sections.blurb: Anthropic prices a record $81 billion IPO, two critical HTTP/2 flaws are patched in Nginx, Vance holds meetings on a week of US outages, Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, and Nvidia's board rules out Jensen Huang's return.

stories.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, raising about $81.3 billion, and its shares start trading on Nasdaq today.
stories.summary: Anthropic set the price on 18 November above its $70 to $78 range and sold about 980 million shares. CNBC reports a fully diluted value of about $1.5 trillion, and trading under the ticker ANT starts on 19 November.
stories.heat: HN 39 pts / 16 comments (low, posted late) · Anthropic (primary), CNBC, CNN, Forbes, PBS NewsHour, Yahoo Finance · velocity: very high, first trading day is today
detail: Anthropic announced on 18 November 2026 that it priced its initial public offering at $83.00 a share. The offering is 980,000,000 Class A shares: 956,351,354 sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 sold by existing stockholders. Trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT is set to begin on 19 November, and the deal is set to close on 20 November. The underwriters have a 30-day option to buy up to 147,000,000 more shares.

The price is above the $70 to $78 range in the amended filing, and the deal was upsized from the 825 million shares planned earlier, CNBC reports. CNBC puts the money raised at $81.3 billion and the fully diluted market value at about $1.5 trillion. CNBC says Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and AMD agreed to invest a combined $26 billion at the IPO price.

CNBC and Forbes call it the largest IPO on record, ahead of SpaceX's listing in June. CNBC's own figures show SpaceX raised $75 billion at first and $85.7 billion with its over-allotment, so the record holds against SpaceX's initial sale only.

Risks named in the coverage: CNBC reports a $104 billion net loss for the nine months to 30 September, mostly from fair-value changes in convertible notes and derivatives, more than 90 pages of risk factors, and two public disputes with the US government this year. CNBC also notes the deal comes during a week of US tech outages and after the exit of Nvidia's chief executive.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are named in Anthropic's release as the contacts for the final prospectus. No first-day trading price was available when this edition was written.

stories.title: Two critical HTTP/2 flaws in Nginx allow unauthenticated remote code execution, and F5 has released fixes.
stories.summary: Wiz Research and four other teams found a use-after-free and an integer underflow in Nginx's HTTP/2 code, both rated CVSS 9.2. Fixed versions are 1.30.7 and 1.31.9, and disabling HTTP/2 is the stopgap.
stories.heat: HN 1137 pts / 508 comments, rank 1 of the day (max 1137) · Wiz (primary), Tenable, Ubuntu security, Safe Security, Brandefense · velocity: high, disclosed 18 November with patching under way
detail: F5 published a security release for Nginx on 18 November 2026 with coordinated disclosure of two HTTP/2 bugs, Wiz reports. CVE-2026-123633 is a use-after-free in HTTP/2 connection handling when Nginx works as a reverse proxy. CVE-2026-123007 is an integer underflow in the HTTP/2 send window that leads to an invalid memory copy. Both are rated critical at CVSS 4.0 9.2 and can be triggered without authentication.

Wiz lists 1.19.7 to 1.31.8 as affected for CVE-2026-123633 and 1.9.5 to 1.31.8 for CVE-2026-123007. Fixed open-source versions are 1.30.7 (stable) and 1.31.9 (mainline). Nginx Plus fixes are 37.0.7.1 and 37.2.0.1 for the first bug, and 37.0.8.1 and 37.3.0.1 for the second. Wiz says the same release fixes other critical Nginx bugs, including CVE-2026-121810 and CVE-2026-123634. Tenable calls the set of five bugs "NGINX2Root".

Wiz says it built working exploits in a lab but will not publish them, and it reports no attacks in the wild so far. Other write-ups say code execution for the use-after-free needs ASLR to be off or bypassed. The flaws were reported to F5 by Wiz Research, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7 and Xint.

If an upgrade is not possible at once, Wiz advises setting "http2 off;" in affected server blocks (Nginx 1.25.1 or later), removing http2 from listen directives and reloading. F5 lists no official mitigation other than the upgrade, according to one write-up. Hacker News commenters discussed how many internet-facing servers run Nginx with HTTP/2 on by default.

stories.title: Vice President Vance cancels a public appearance to hold meetings on a week of US tech outages, which officials say are not linked.
stories.summary: Outages hit the FAA, Microsoft, the NSA, JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines and Apple within about a week. Officials blame upgrades and patches, while an anonymously sourced report says rushed fixes for AI-found flaws caused them.
stories.heat: no HN thread in the top 30 · CNBC, Fortune, The Next Web, Washington Sun, Daily Wire · velocity: high, congressional testimony on 18 November and new reports overnight
detail: JD Vance cancelled his appearance at The New York Times DealBook Summit on 18 November 2026 to attend meetings on the outages, CNBC reports. The list in CNBC's report: a nationwide aviation ground stop, a long Microsoft Outlook outage, a reported blackout of the NSA's classified network, software problems at JPMorgan Chase, a United Airlines outage that delayed flights, and problems with Apple services.

A senior administration official told reporters there is no sign of a cyberattack or coordinated action, and put the incidents down to upgrades, patching, hardware changes or "disparate" events. Asked how far AI was involved, the official said it is "challenging to answer that question across all of these incidents". Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee on 18 November: "We have no indication that these incidents are related, that they're coordinated."

The Washington Sun, citing three anonymous sources, reported that bank executives and NSA officials told members of Congress that the outages broadly came from attempts to patch vulnerabilities found by AI, The Next Web reports. Chase and Microsoft have given other technical causes in public, and a Rapid7 researcher told Bloomberg he sees no public evidence for the patching theory. This claim is unconfirmed.
Senator Mark Warner called for a "pre-testing regime" for new AI models, CNBC reports. The previous edition covered the Apple and NSA outages on their own.

stories.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, a mid-size model priced at $3 per million input tokens, which Google says leads a coding-agent ranking.
stories.summary: Google released Neon on 18 November between its Carbon and Hydrogen models, with a 1 million token context window. Artificial Analysis scores it 61, third overall, and VentureBeat notes Google gives no absolute times for its "3x faster" claim.
stories.heat: HN 434 pts / 412 comments, rank 5 of the day (max 1137), plus a 50 pt follow-up post · Google (primary), VentureBeat, Artificial Analysis, Interesting Engineering, TestingCatalog · velocity: high, launched 18 November
detail: Google released Gemini 4 Neon on 18 November 2026 for software engineering, knowledge work and science. It sits between Gemini 4 Carbon, for the hardest long tasks, and Gemini 4 Hydrogen, for fast everyday work. It is rolling out in the paid Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Android Studio, Antigravity and the Gemini app for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

Prices from Google: $3 per million input tokens, $0.15 per million cached input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million token context window. VentureBeat says that is 25% lower than Claude Opus 5.5 on API tokens.

Google's benchmark claims include first place on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index at 58.6, 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and second on the Vals Index at 70.9%. Artificial Analysis scores Neon (xhigh) at 61 on its Intelligence Index, 1 point above Gemini 4 Carbon, at about 17% lower cost per task, and calls it Google's fourth model in seven weeks.

VentureBeat reports that Claude Opus 5.5 narrowly beats Neon on Terminal-Bench 4.1, 65.8% to 65.2%, and that Google's "three times faster" claim against Carbon comes without absolute completion times. Hacker News commenters compared it with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol on price.

stories.title: Nvidia's board says it will not reinstate Jensen Huang, after Huang says he would be "honored" to return.
stories.summary: Board chair Harvey Jones said on the earnings call that the board does not intend to bring Huang back. CNBC reports a petition for his return with nearly 200,000 signatures, and Nvidia has stopped shipping licensed Hopper chips to China.
stories.heat: no HN thread in the top 30 · CNBC, Yahoo Finance, Daily Caller, Crypto Briefing · velocity: high, Kress held her first all-hands on 18 November
detail: In his first public statement, on 17 November 2026, Jensen Huang said he would be "honored" to return to Nvidia, CNBC reports. Board chair Harvey Jones said on the earnings call: "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Interim chief executive Colette Kress repeated this to CNBC's Jim Cramer.

Kress held her first company-wide all-hands meeting on 18 November. An attendee told CNBC her message was "Let's move forward." CNBC reports an online petition for Huang's return with nearly 200,000 signatures, more than 10,000 of them from people who say they are current employees, out of about 42,000 staff. The Wall Street Journal reported a letter from senior engineer Nader Khalil warning the board it could lose "irreplaceable talent".

On China, Kress said on the earnings call that Nvidia has stopped shipping licensed Hopper chips there, and Nvidia said it assumes no China data-centre compute revenue in its outlook, per Yahoo Finance. The Daily Caller puts the Hopper sales to China in the fiscal third quarter at $2.4 billion. Nvidia did not say whether the stop is permanent. The previous edition covered the earnings figures.

stories.title: Waymo stops freeway rides in all its markets after California's DMV calls them an "imminent hazard to public safety".
stories.summary: The DMV order of 11 November became public on 17 November and cites robotaxis entering a construction closure on US 101. Surface-street rides continue, and there is no end date.
stories.heat: no HN thread in the top 30 · TechCrunch, Washington Post, Engadget, ABC7, TechRepublic, Motor1 · velocity: moderate to high, order made public 17 November
detail: California's DMV issued restrictions on Waymo's driverless freeway operations on 11 November 2026, and they became public on 17 November, TechCrunch reports. The DMV cited three Waymo robotaxis entering an active construction closure on US Route 101 near Burlingame and a separate incident with California Highway Patrol vehicles on Highway 280 in San Francisco. It said the incursions happened despite corrective actions after similar incidents on 18 May. Waymo says there were no injuries or collisions on US 101.

Waymo has paused freeway rides in every market, including those outside California. Spokesperson Dana Gallagher said the company is working with the DMV to resume. Rides on surface streets continue, which TechCrunch says total over half a million trips a week across 15 US cities. The restriction stays until Waymo shows "effective corrective actions".
This is Waymo's second freeway pause this year: it stopped in May and returned in July after a software update for construction zones, TechCrunch reports.

stories.title: Congressional auditors at the GAO got four major AI chatbots to help plan terror attacks in covert tests.
stories.summary: The Washington Post reports that the GAO tested chatbots from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and SpaceXAI and got past their safeguards. The companies say the tests used older models, and the GAO says its sample is not statistically significant.
stories.heat: no HN thread in the top 30 · Washington Post, Fortune, AP via EMS1, WMUR, Yahoo News · velocity: moderate, report published 18 November
detail: The Washington Post reported on 18 November 2026 that the Government Accountability Office ran covert tests on chatbots from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and SpaceXAI. The safeguards first blocked the auditors, who later got past them. Fortune reports that two of the bots produced plans for an explosive device aimed at mass casualties and two produced plans against the electrical grid.

A GAO official said the testing is not "a statistically significant sample", and the GAO made no recommendations. The companies said the tests used older model versions and that protections have been strengthened since. Anthropic told the AP it could not verify the GAO's results. Senator Maggie Hassan, who requested the report, said the threat is no longer theoretical.

stories.title: KPMG UK says more than 100 AI agents went deeper than its human auditors in some areas of a trial audit.
stories.summary: The trial, called Project Exponential, ran alongside a real audit of an unnamed FTSE 250 company and was not used to approve its accounts. One agent mismatched regulatory rules and an auditor had to step in.
stories.heat: HN 354 pts / 160 comments, rank 6 of the day (max 1137) · Financial Times (paywall), European Business Magazine · velocity: moderate, reported 18 November
detail: The Financial Times reported, and European Business Magazine republished on 18 November 2026, that KPMG UK ran more than 100 AI agents on an audit of an unnamed FTSE 250 company. The agents collected and analysed data, drafted conclusions, suggested next steps and split up tasks between them. KPMG UK head of audit Cath Burnet said the technology had "gone considerably deeper into issues" in several cases and asked questions the human team had not raised.

It was an experiment: an audit partner signed it off, but its findings were not the basis for approving the accounts. One agent failed to match regulatory requirements to the company's documents and needed a human to step in. KPMG plans to extend the trial to up to 20 larger audits and says the technology is not ready for thousands of engagements. No figures on errors or issues found were published. The UK Financial Reporting Council has warned that AI must not weaken auditor independence or scepticism.

stories.title: Oregon sues OpenAI for about $2 billion, alleging that ChatGPT was marketed as safe for children without adequate safeguards.
stories.summary: Attorney General Dan Rayfield filed the case on 17 November under Oregon's consumer protection law. OpenAI says it keeps working with experts on safeguards, and none of the claims have been tested in court.
stories.heat: no HN thread in the top 30 · KLCC, Quartz, TechRepublic, Daily Caller, Lookout Eugene-Springfield · velocity: moderate, filed 17 November
detail: Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield sued OpenAI on 17 November 2026 in Multnomah County Circuit Court under the state's Unlawful Trade Practices Act, KLCC reports. Several outlets put the claim at $2.035 billion. The state alleges that OpenAI presented ChatGPT as safe for children, kept marketing it to minors without adequate guardrails, and that ChatGPT often failed to alert linked parents during a child's mental health emergency.

Oregon asks for stronger protections, more reliable age verification and clearer information for parents, and wants a jury trial. OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company is committed to working with experts on more safeguards. Reports differ on how many other states have sued OpenAI.

stories.title: Palo Alto Networks agrees to buy the AI model training start-up Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock.
stories.summary: The deal was announced on 18 November with Palo Alto's fiscal first-quarter results, which beat estimates. Applied Compute's chief executive Yash Patil will become Palo Alto's co-chief AI officer.
stories.heat: HN 8 pts · Bloomberg, SEC 8-K (primary), Benzinga, Calcalist, Yahoo Finance · velocity: moderate, announced 18 November
detail: Palo Alto Networks said on 18 November 2026 that it will acquire Applied Compute in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion, Bloomberg reports, with closing expected in Palo Alto's fiscal third quarter and subject to regulatory clearance. Palo Alto plans to use the technology so companies can train and deploy open-weight models with security built in. Co-founder Yash Patil said on X that Applied Compute went from zero to over $100 million in annualised revenue in just over 18 months, a company claim.
Palo Alto also reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of about $3.45 billion against estimates of $3.31 billion and raised its full-year forecast, Yahoo Finance reports.
stories.about: Applied Compute is a start-up that helps companies post-train and serve open-weight AI models on their own data.

stories.title: Google DeepMind opens Genie 4, its interactive world model with real-time audio, to Google AI Ultra subscribers.
stories.summary: Users can change weather, add characters or redirect the action with new prompts during a session. AI Pro members can join a waitlist, and Google lists scene permanence and physics as open problems.
stories.heat: HN 186 pts / 143 comments, rank 9 of the day (max 1137) · Google (primary) · velocity: moderate, launched 18 November
detail: Google made Genie 4 available on 18 November 2026 in Project Genie for eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers, with a waitlist for AI Pro. It is the first Genie model with native real-time audio that adapts to the scene, and it accepts new prompts mid-session. A Project Genie agent can build worlds through conversation, and a community gallery lets users publish and remix them.

Google lists camera latency, complex physical interactions, audio precision and long-term scene permanence as open challenges, and gives no time limits for Genie 4. Genie 3 stays available, with runs now up to 3 minutes. All output carries SynthID watermarks.

stories.title: At Ignite, Microsoft adds six more in-house AI models beyond MAI Code 2 and says its Maia 200 chip is in production.
stories.summary: The new models cover security, images, live speech, transcription and routing, and Microsoft compares each on price with OpenAI and Anthropic models. All the figures are Microsoft's own.
stories.heat: HN 449 pts / 311 comments, rank 4 of the day (max 1137) · Microsoft AI (primary) · velocity: moderate, Ignite announcements of 17 November still discussed
detail: Microsoft's Ignite post of 17 November 2026 lists seven models. Beyond MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash, which the previous edition covered, they are MAI Cyber 2 Flash for codebase-scale security work, MAI Image 2.7, the speech-to-speech model MAI Realtime 1 from $0.01 per audio minute, Dragon Copilot Transcribe for clinical notes, and Decision 1.1, which routes work to larger models only when needed.

Microsoft claims MAI Cyber 2 Flash matches GPT-6 Astra on the CyberGym-E2E benchmark at under 2% of the cost per task, and that Decision 1.1 is 50 times faster and 79 times cheaper than GPT-6.1 Sol. It also says its second-generation Maia 200 accelerator is in production with 1.7 times more tokens per watt. None of these claims have been tested independently.

stories.title: OpenAI says its models improved chip designs for AMD and for its own Jalapeño inference chip.
stories.summary: OpenAI reports up to a 14% gain in power, performance and area on AMD flagship GPU design blocks and about 13% less area in Jalapeño's vector unit. The results are OpenAI's own and have not been independently checked.
stories.heat: HN 161 pts / 101 comments, rank 12 of the day (max 1137) · OpenAI (primary, 403 to our fetcher), Sina Finance, 17173, Shattered · velocity: moderate, posted 18 November
detail: OpenAI published "Advancing chip design with OpenAI models" on 18 November 2026. According to coverage of the post, its models rewrote SystemVerilog RTL to cut the area of the vector unit in Jalapeño, its first custom inference chip, by about 13%, and gave up to a 14% gain in power, performance and area on AMD's flagship GPU IP against a heavily optimised baseline. Some changes went into a design already sent for manufacturing.

OpenAI says this compressed about a year of design progress into under five months, and that it is working with Synopsys on a model called GPT-Synopsys that uses chip design tools. We could not open the OpenAI page directly, so this card rests on search summaries of it.

stories.title: A Linux KVM flaw, CVE-2026-99312, can leave a stale memory context in nested virtualisation on AMD processors.
stories.summary: The bug affects nested SVM on AMD hardware only, and the upstream fix was committed on 2 November. Trackers disagree on severity, and one write-up claims a guest-to-host escape.
stories.heat: HN 174 pts / 115 comments, rank 10 of the day (max 1137) · CVE.org, Rapid7, OpenCVE, Kernelscan, LowEndSpirit · velocity: moderate, CVE published 18 November
detail: CVE-2026-99312 was published on 18 November 2026. If an INIT is emulated while a nested (L2) guest runs with paging disabled, KVM can keep running the L1 guest with a stale MMU context. Trackers say only nested SVM on AMD is affected, not Intel VMX. The upstream fix, "KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT", was committed by Paolo Bonzini on 2 November.

Severity ratings differ: one tracker lists Medium and Kernelscan lists High, needing a privileged user in an L1 guest with nested virtualisation on. One secondary write-up describes a working guest-to-host exploit that reads and writes host memory, which no other source confirms. Red Hat lists the fix as deferred for RHEL 10, per one tracker. Hosting providers that offer nested virtualisation on AMD are most exposed.

stories.title: Ruby fixes seven memory-safety bugs in regular expressions and string case conversion, some of which allow remote code execution.
stories.summary: The fixed versions are Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14. Ruby 3.2 and earlier are end of life and get no fix.
stories.heat: HN 60 pts / 11 comments · ruby-lang.org (primary) · velocity: low, a security notice of 18 November
detail: The Ruby team published an advisory on 18 November 2026 for seven bugs, tracked by GitHub advisory IDs while CVEs are pending. They include heap buffer overflows and a double free in regex compilation and string case conversion. The advisory says proof-of-concept code exists for some, and the risk is highest for applications that compile or match attacker-supplied regex patterns or change the case of crafted strings.
Affected: Ruby 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0 to 3.4.12 and 4.0.0 to 4.0.9. Fixed: 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14.

stories.title: Trump holds talks with Xi in Shenzhen before the first three-way meeting with Putin, and a separate Trump-Putin meeting is now confirmed.
stories.summary: On Thursday 19 November, Trump and Xi Jinping meet one to one before Putin joins them for the first US-China-Russia leaders' meeting, on the sidelines of APEC. No outcome had been reported as of early Thursday, and North Korean state media suggested Kim Jong-un will not meet Trump in China (NBC, Nikkei Asia, Korea Times).
stories.heat: Live blogs at NBC, ABC, Fox and Nikkei Asia; AP, CNBC, Fortune, Korea Times and Xinhua carrying the day; lead item on ABC's international page · velocity: high, meetings under way this morning
detail: What is new since the last edition: Trump arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday 18 November, and Xi greeted him at the foot of Air Force One, a gesture NBC called rare for a Chinese leader. Xi said this returned Trump's greeting when Xi visited the US in September (CNBC). Trump then attended a welcome banquet with Marco Rubio, Scott Bessent and Howard Lutnick.

A US official confirmed to ABC on 18 November that Trump and Putin will meet one to one on Thursday, although a senior official had said earlier that 'there's no bilateral scheduled'. NBC called it their first in-person meeting in more than a year. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said: 'The meeting will happen, the meeting will happen.' Trump, Putin and Xi shook hands together at the APEC opening.

Xi sets a trade agenda. At the APEC opening and the banquet he called for free trade, cooperation on artificial intelligence and 'concrete results' on openness and innovation (CNBC, Nikkei Asia). Putin, after his own talks with Xi on Wednesday, said sanctions on Russia had backfired and made the country stronger (CNBC). Xi told Putin it was their '50th personal meeting' (NBC).

For the Trump-Xi meeting, the Korea Times lists tariffs, rare-earth export controls and chip restrictions. Fortune notes that the current trade truce runs out on 10 January 2027 and that a new US rule of 16 November requires licences for advanced AI chips sent to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, which Beijing says it will answer with countermeasures. Trump told Fox News on Thursday morning that he and Xi had discussed AI and that Nvidia's Jensen Huang came up only 'briefly' (Nikkei Asia, 9:40 a.m. Shenzhen time).

Expectations remain low. A senior US official said 'We do not expect to get to any kind of agreement', and Ushakov said a joint statement was still being drafted; if none is agreed, each side will give its own account (Korea Times). On North Korea, Rubio said on 17 November that no Trump-Kim meeting was scheduled: 'It may not happen, but he's prepared to do it.' NBC reported on 18 November that North Korean state media suggested Kim would not come.

stories.title: The International Court of Justice gives its judgment today on whether Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya.
stories.summary: The UN's top court in The Hague rules on Thursday 19 November in the case The Gambia filed against Myanmar in 2019. AP says a genocide finding would be the first of its kind by this court, and the ruling is final but cannot be enforced by the court itself (AP, Al Jazeera).
stories.heat: AP, Al Jazeera, Deccan Herald, HRW and Physicians for Human Rights previews; on ABC's international page · velocity: rising, verdict due at 10:00 Hague time
stories.about: The Gambia, a Muslim-majority West African country, brought the case under the 1948 Genocide Convention with the backing of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation.
detail: The court's case page lists the judgment for Thursday 19 November 2026 at 10 a.m. at the Peace Palace in The Hague. The case concerns Myanmar's 2017 military campaign in Rakhine State, which Myanmar calls a legitimate counter-terrorism operation (AP).

The Gambia asks the court to declare that Myanmar committed and conspired to commit genocide and failed to prevent or punish it, and to order prosecutions, safe return, restored property, recognition of the Rohingya identity and compensation, including full citizenship (AP, Al Jazeera). The key legal question, Al Jazeera reports, is whether Myanmar intended to destroy the Rohingya as a group.

About 1.2 million Rohingya live as refugees in Bangladesh, mostly in the Cox's Bazar camps (Al Jazeera). In 2022 the court ruled 15 to 1 that it had jurisdiction. The judgment is final and binding, but if Myanmar ignores it the court can only report this to the UN Security Council, where a veto can block action.
