stories.title: House Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be the first Black Speaker of the US House.
stories.summary: In a closed-door caucus vote on 18 November, Jeffries won 251 of 262 ballots, with 11 no votes, after the Democrats won the House on 3 November. The floor vote is due in January (ABC News).
stories.heat: ABC, NBC and other US networks; ABC navigation headline · velocity: steady, the result was expected
detail: ABC News reported on 18 November that 251 Democrats voted for Jeffries and 11 voted no in a secret ballot. Seven progressive members said they voted no because 'there is still work to be done'. Jeffries needs 218 votes on the House floor in January; ABC projects 257 Democratic seats against 171 Republican.

The caucus also elected Katherine Clark as majority leader, the first woman in that post, and Pete Aguilar as majority whip, the first Latino in that post. Ted Lieu becomes caucus chair. Jeffries said the economy will be central to his leadership: 'We hear you. We see you. We feel you.'

stories.title: Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi meets Putin in Shenzhen and asks him to free a detained Japanese journalist.
stories.summary: Takaichi and Putin talked for about 30 minutes on 18 November on the APEC sidelines, the first in-person meeting of the two countries' leaders since 2022. She asked for the release of Hokkaido Shimbun journalist Yuki Imai, and both sides agreed only to keep talking (Nikkei Asia, SCMP).
stories.heat: Nikkei Asia, SCMP, Jiji and Japanese media; all details come from the Japanese side · velocity: moderate
detail: Nikkei Asia reports that Takaichi pressed for Imai's release and for Russia to reverse measures against Japan Tobacco's Russian subsidiaries. Imai has been held for more than a month on alleged espionage charges. A Japanese official said the two leaders agreed to keep communicating 'at various levels' but did not say how Putin answered.
No joint statement was issued. On the evening of 18 November, Takaichi and Xi Jinping shook hands at the APEC banquet, but Nikkei Asia reported no talks between them.

stories.title: COP31 negotiators in Antalya wait for a revised deal text with one day left before the summit is due to close.
stories.summary: The talks are due to end on Friday 20 November, and countries are still split over the draft text's call to 'phase out' fossil fuels and over a proposed adaptation finance target of at least $120 billion (RTE, technology.org).
stories.heat: RTE, Reuters-based reports, Rio Times and climate press · velocity: rising toward the deadline
detail: The first draft of the main 'cover decision', published on Monday 16 November, ran to 18 pages. It holds two paragraphs side by side: one urges faster action on the 2023 Dubai pledge to 'transition away from' fossil fuels, and the other calls for faster efforts to 'phase out' fossil fuels; either could be removed (RTE). Australia's Chris Bowen, who leads the negotiations, said there would be 'at least one more draft' this week.

On money, the draft proposes a collective adaptation target of at least $120 billion. The EU opposes new financial commitments. The UN Environment Programme puts developing countries' adaptation needs at about $305 billion a year by 2035, against $28 billion to $32 billion of public adaptation funding from rich countries in 2024. The EU signed up on 17 November to Turkey's voluntary target for electricity to supply 35% of global energy use by 2035, up from about 23% today (RTE).

stories.title: Police in Bangladesh fire tear gas at thousands of garment workers who want the monthly minimum wage raised to 30,000 taka.
stories.summary: Workers clashed with police on 18 November in Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur near Dhaka, and about 25 factories in Ashulia closed. They want the minimum wage raised from 12,500 taka (about $98) to 30,000 taka (about $236) (AP).
stories.heat: AP wire, carried by ABC News; Bangladeshi media · velocity: escalating, hundreds of factories shut in recent weeks
detail: AP reports that police used tear gas, stun grenades and batons, that protesters set fire to a police vehicle in Gazipur and threw stones in Ashulia, and that workers blocked the Dhaka-Aricha highway in Savar. Local media put the crowd at one factory at about 20,000. The number of injured was not clear.

Bangladesh's garment industry earns about $40 billion a year from exports and employs about 4 million people directly, most of them women from rural areas, in about 2,500 factories. A wage board formed by the government has not yet produced a package that satisfies the workers (AP).

stories.title: Papua New Guinea's prime minister tells Xi Jinping that closing Taiwan's office in his country 'wasn't easy'.
stories.summary: James Marape told Xi at APEC on 17 November that Taiwan no longer operates in Papua New Guinea, and China agreed to buy more of its gas. Taiwan had said in early November that it would close its de facto embassy in Port Moresby, and it blamed Chinese pressure (Reuters via US News, Taipei Times).
stories.heat: Reuters, Taipei Times, ThePrint, AsiaOne, Nikkei Asia · velocity: moderate
detail: Marape said: 'I faced challenges from within, because we also relate to many nations, but we were resolved' (Reuters). Xi thanked him for keeping to the 'one China' principle. The US State Department called the closure 'yet another example of Beijing's intimidation campaign against Taiwan'.

Other APEC sideline deals with Xi: on 17 November, Canada's Mark Carney and Xi agreed to extend and widen a preliminary trade deal that gives tariff relief on about C$400 million of Canadian exports (Nikkei Asia). Taiwan is represented in Shenzhen by Stan Shih, not by President Lai Ching-te.

stories.title: UK inflation rises to 3.6% in October, its highest in a year, which makes a second Bank of England rate rise in December more likely.
stories.summary: Annual inflation rose from 3.5% in September as fuel prices climbed because of the Iran war and disruption in the Strait of Hormuz. The Bank of England raised its rate to 4% earlier in November (AP).
stories.heat: AP wire, UK national press · velocity: one-day data story
detail: AP reports that the Bank of England expects inflation to peak at about 5% next summer, against its 2% target. One economist told AP: 'These figures make a December rate hike look difficult to avoid.' Brent crude has fallen to about $92 a barrel from about $110 earlier in the month, which could lower that peak.

stories.title: A Mongolian parliamentary committee backs President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh's request to resign, and the full parliament votes next.
stories.summary: The Standing Committee on State Structure endorsed the request on 18 November, the day after Khurelsukh announced it. If parliament accepts, the speaker takes over the president's powers and an election must be called within four months (Xinhua).
stories.heat: Xinhua, Bloomberg, Manila Times, AsiaNews · velocity: slowing
detail: Khurelsukh announced his resignation on 17 November after the opposition Democratic Party accused him of graft and threatened impeachment; he denies wrongdoing. Xinhua says the 126-member parliament will consider the request at its next plenary session, with no date given. Reports describe it as the first time a sitting Mongolian president has asked to resign.

sections.title: Krieg
sections.blurb: Iran hits Kuwait's Ali Al Salem base, Israeli troops cross Gaza's Yellow Line, Ukraine strikes two Krasnodar refineries, the Saudi coalition bombs 60 Houthi sites, and CENTCOM widens the Iran blockade to ship-to-ship transfers, and security forces kill a Lashkar commander in Kulgam.

stories.title: Iran fired drones at the US-used Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait on 18 November, its first attack on Kuwait in about two months.
stories.summary: Iran's army said it hit Patriot air defences and drone and missile launch sites at the base after a US strike on Qeshm Island; Kuwait said it intercepted the drones and reported no damage (AP). Bahrain said it intercepted several Iranian attacks the same morning.
stories.heat: Ground News lead story · AP/PBS, Fox News, Korea Times, IranWire, NewsNation · velocity: high, Iran widened its targets from Bahrain to Kuwait
detail: Early on Wednesday 18 November, Iran targeted Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait. Iranian state television said the strikes were aimed at air defence systems and at drone and missile launch platforms. Kuwait's military said its air defences intercepted the drones and reported no immediate damage, and Kuwait's Foreign Ministry called the attacks "criminal" (AP via PBS). Fox News reported these were Iran's first attacks on Kuwait in more than two months.

Bahrain, home of the US Navy's 5th Fleet, said it intercepted "several Iranian aerial attacks". Its Interior Ministry issued two shelter alerts and then an all-clear. It gave no damage or casualty figures (AP).

The trigger, by both sides' accounts: on Tuesday 17 November Iran attacked a US radar at Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain, and a US fighter jet then struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. A US official said the Qeshm strike was "in response to IRGC aggression targeting U.S. personnel and assets" (Fox News). Iran says its attacks answer US drone surveillance and an attack on Iranian communications towers (AP).

Neither government has published independent damage details for the Kuwait strike, so Iran's claims of hits are unverified. AP counts at least 30 strikes on Ali Al Salem during the war, with at least 15 hangars damaged or destroyed.

Trump has said new US strikes are highly unlikely, but he has sent a third aircraft carrier and thousands more troops to the region, AP reported. Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper met Israel's army chief Eyal Zamir and Mossad director Roman Gofman in Tel Aviv.

stories.title: Israeli troops crossed the Yellow Line into Hamas-held central Gaza on 18 November to destroy a tunnel, the first such armoured push since the 2025 ceasefire.
stories.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet said the tunnel near Nuseirat posed an immediate threat to troops, and COGAT ordered residents of parts of Bureij and Nuseirat to leave (Times of Israel). Hamas called it a flagrant violation of the ceasefire.
stories.heat: Times of Israel, JNS, BBC, AFP via NST and GMA, TASS · velocity: high, first crossing of the line in about 13 months
detail: On Wednesday 18 November the Israeli military said it had begun "targeted operational activity" to destroy a tunnel west of the Yellow Line, the line that has separated Israeli-held and Hamas-held Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire. Palestinian media reported tanks and armoured vehicles advancing there for the first time since the truce, and Salah al-Din Road was to be closed in the area (Times of Israel).

COGAT told residents of blocks 660, 661 and 666 in the Bureij and Nuseirat areas to leave for the duration of the operation. A Gaza security source told AFP of "intense Israeli artillery shelling" north of Nuseirat. No casualty figures for the operation had been published.

Hamas called the advance "a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement". A day earlier the IDF said it killed two Hamas platoon commanders in Khan Younis and Jabalia, saying they were planning attacks.

The US-backed Board of Peace warned on Tuesday that the ceasefire could collapse without full implementation and criticised Israeli delays and restrictions on winter shelter equipment; Hamas official Basem Naim called its report "pure disinformation" (Times of Israel). Gaza's Hamas-run health officials say more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire; Israel says five of its soldiers have been killed in that time.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones hit the Ilsky and Afipsky oil refineries in Russia's Krasnodar Krai overnight into 18 November, Ukraine's General Staff says.
stories.summary: Krasnodar officials said nine people were injured and a damaged gas pipeline cut supply to 94 apartment buildings (Kyiv Independent). Both refineries have been hit repeatedly in recent months.
stories.heat: Kyiv Independent, Meduza, Moscow Times, Ukrinform, Militarnyi, NV · velocity: moderate, part of a run of refinery strikes
detail: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed strikes on the Ilsky refinery, where it said oil tanks were damaged, and on the Afipsky refinery, where it said a processing plant was hit. Both are in the Seversky district of Krasnodar Krai. It did not say which weapons were used (Kyiv Independent).

Krasnodar Krai's operational headquarters blamed falling drone debris for fires and said nine people were injured, one of them hospitalised. Debris damaged homes and commercial buildings, and a damaged gas pipeline cut supply to 94 apartment buildings. The Kyiv Independent said it could not independently verify the damage or the injuries. Euromaidan Press noted the strikes came a day before Putin's meeting with Trump and Xi in Shenzhen.

stories.title: The Saudi-led coalition says it struck 60 Houthi military targets in northern Yemen and intercepted two cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh.
stories.summary: Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said strikes on 17 November hit Sanaa, Hodeidah, Amran and Saada, while fighting resumed at Tur al-Baha on the road to Aden (Al Jazeera). The Houthis said they targeted oil pumping stations near Riyadh.
stories.heat: Al Jazeera, AP (via US stations), PBS · velocity: high, the Houthi push on Aden is now drawing strikes on Saudi Arabia
detail: Al-Maliki said on Wednesday 18 November that coalition forces carried out a "precision operation" against 60 Houthi military targets the day before, destroying tunnels used as workshops and storage for ballistic missiles. The coalition also said it intercepted two Houthi cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh on Wednesday, and alerts sounded in Jizan, Najran and Khamis Mushait (Al Jazeera).

Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed the group targeted oil pumping stations near Riyadh and a radar site in southern Saudi Arabia; Saudi authorities had not responded. On the ground, Al Jazeera's reporter in Taiz described "fierce battles" at Tur al-Baha in Lahij, about 80 to 85 km from Aden, after government forces pulled back from Dhubab and the Bab al-Mandeb area. AP reported that Saudi officials told allies the war with the Houthis could last six more months.

stories.title: US Central Command says ships that take Iranian cargo in ship-to-ship transfers at sea may be treated as running the blockade of Iran.
stories.summary: The 18 November advisory says such ships can be stopped, boarded, diverted or captured, even if they never enter an Iranian port (Reuters via gCaptain). Neutral transit of the Strait of Hormuz is not affected, CENTCOM says.
stories.heat: Reuters via gCaptain, Arab News, EnergyNow, Samaa · velocity: rising, closes a route Iran has used for LPG and jet fuel
detail: The advisory says any vessel that receives cargo by ship-to-ship transfer from a blockaded vessel carrying cargo loaded in Iran may be considered to be evading the blockade. Such ships may be stopped, boarded, diverted, captured or sent to the Iranian port where the cargo came from, and ships that do not comply could face enforcement "including the use of force consistent with applicable law" (Reuters, reported by Jonathan Saul).

The US blockade of Iranian ports was first imposed on 13 April, lifted in June after a draft understanding, and reimposed on 14 July when that collapsed. Shipping sources told Reuters that Iran has still exported some LPG and jet fuel since July, while its crude exports have been near a standstill for months.

stories.title: Security forces killed Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat in a mosque in Kulgam, and Amit Shah called him the group's last known active local militant in the Kashmir valley.
stories.summary: Bhat, 22, was killed early on 18 November in Zangalpora after an eight-day search and a refused offer to surrender by video call; police linked him to the 11 November attack that injured three CRPF personnel (The Wire, Deccan Herald).
stories.heat: The Wire, Deccan Herald, The Tribune, Kashmir Images, KNS, Google News India top story · Amit Shah statement · velocity: high on 18 November
detail: Mohammad Lateef Bhat, 22, of Khrewan village, was killed in the early hours of Wednesday 18 November in Zangalpora village in the Devsar area of Kulgam district, south Kashmir, The Wire reports. Police say he opened fire from inside a mosque at about 2:45 am. Kashmir Police said a body and a weapon were recovered. Reports say 27 civilians were moved out of an adjoining seminary before troops fired tear gas into the mosque.

The cordon and search operation lasted eight days. On 16 November an encounter at the Laru bypass killed Umar Nisar Dar, a baker who was not a listed militant and whom agencies suspect joined Bhat in the 11 November attack on a CRPF party at Nowpora Akhran; early reports had wrongly named the dead man as Bhat. Police had offered Rs 15 lakh for information on Bhat. Kulgam SSP Anayat Ali said he spoke to Bhat by video call and urged him to surrender, and called the operation potentially one of the biggest successes of the year (The Wire).

Union Home Minister Amit Shah praised the police, Army, CRPF and intelligence agencies and called Bhat "Lashkar's last known active local terrorist in the valley". Police say Bhat joined in November 2025 and was tied to a Lashkar shadow group (The Wire). Political leaders across parties criticised the hardship the long searches caused residents in the cold.

stories.title: An ADNOC-operated tanker was attacked north of Khasab with 11 crew injured and one missing, while the LPG carrier Tara Gas was still burning off Oman on 18 November.
stories.summary: ADNOC Logistics and Services reported the 17 November attack on its tanker, which Vanguard Tech named as the Navig8 Messi (gCaptain). A navigation warning on 18 November said Tara Gas was on fire and adrift about 5.7 nautical miles off Oman.
stories.heat: gCaptain, AP, UKMTO warnings · velocity: moderate, a second ship hit in two days in the same waters
detail: UKMTO said the ADNOC-operated tanker was struck on the evening of 17 November about 13 nautical miles north of Khasab, and that a search continued for one missing crew member. ADNOC said 11 crew were injured and that its "immediate priority is supporting the search and rescue effort". ADNOC did not name the ship; the security firm Vanguard Tech identified it as the Liberian-flagged product tanker Navig8 Messi (gCaptain). No one has claimed the attack; AP said Iran continues to attack tankers in the strait.

Tara Gas, hit on 16 and 17 November, was still burning and drifting on 18 November according to a NAVAREA IX warning, despite some reports that the fire was out. Oman rescued 24 of its 25 crew; one Indian seafarer is missing and India's foreign ministry said two Indian crew are in hospital in Khasab.

stories.title: Zelensky says the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin on 19 November will seek more air defence and energy aid for Ukraine.
stories.summary: The US is represented at the meeting, Zelensky said, and he praised an EU Commission proposal of up to 45 billion euros for Ukraine in 2027 (Kyiv Independent). He said Ukraine's issues must be resolved with Ukraine at the table.
stories.heat: Kyiv Independent, Kyiv Post, Glavnoe · velocity: rising, meets the same day as the Shenzhen summit
detail: Zelensky said the primary aim of the 19 November meeting is extra support for air defence and the energy grid, which Russia is bombing ahead of winter. He called financial aid an important part of the agenda and praised the European Commission's proposal of up to 45 billion euros (about 49.5 billion dollars) for 2027, which EU states have not yet approved (Kyiv Independent).

"The war must end, and Russia will achieve none of its objectives through this war," he said, adding that "issues concerning Ukraine must be resolved with Ukraine's participation." US representatives promised to brief him on Trump's meeting with Xi Jinping and Putin in Shenzhen, the Kyiv Independent reported.

stories.title: Putin and Xi discussed a settlement of the war in Ukraine at their meeting in Shenzhen, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says.
stories.summary: Peskov said on 18 November that Putin briefed Xi on his talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, and that Ukraine could also come up with Trump (APA). Trump, Putin and Xi meet in Shenzhen on 19 November on the sidelines of APEC (CBS News).
stories.heat: CBS News, Kyiv Post, Ukrainska Pravda, APA, Censor.net · velocity: rising into the 19 November trilateral
detail: Peskov gave no details beyond saying the two leaders discussed "the settlement of the Ukraine conflict" and that Putin told Xi about his recent contacts with Witkoff and Kushner (APA). Peskov also said Trump and Putin had an informal meeting on Wednesday (CBS News).

The White House says the three-way meeting on Thursday will focus on nuclear proliferation, and a senior US official said Trump intends to raise Iran. A US official said over the weekend that Ukraine was not expected to be discussed (CBS News). Kyiv has urged Trump and Xi to press Putin to end the war (Kyiv Post).

stories.title: Iran's army says it shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone over the eastern Strait of Hormuz on 18 November; the US has not confirmed it.
stories.summary: The claim came from the Iranian army's public relations office, carried by Tasnim; CENTCOM had not commented. It follows Iranian claims of two MQ-1 shootdowns earlier in the week, also unconfirmed.
stories.heat: Tasnim, Trend, Middle East Eye, Caspian Post · velocity: moderate, the third such claim in four days
detail: Tasnim said on Wednesday 18 November that army air defence systems downed an MQ-9 east of the Strait of Hormuz. US Central Command had not commented, and no independent imagery was published. On 16 November Iran's army claimed an MQ-1 over the strait, and the IRGC claimed a separate MQ-1 south of Qeshm Island (Middle East Eye); the US has confirmed neither.

stories.title: Russian attacks injured three people in Kyiv on 18 November, Mayor Vitali Klitschko says; reports of a drone hitting a 28-storey block in Pechersk conflict.
stories.summary: Klitschko said one person was hospitalised and two were treated as outpatients (Ukrinform). Censor.net reported a Shahed damaged a 28-storey residential block at the 11th floor, but a Ukrinform live item said that report was not confirmed.
stories.heat: Ukrinform, Censor.net, Yahoo News · velocity: low, a daytime attack after the 17 November bridge strikes
detail: Klitschko posted on Telegram: "Three people have been injured in the capital today." Yahoo News reported debris from downed drones fell in three Kyiv districts. Censor.net said a Shahed crashed in the Pechersk district and damaged a 28-storey residential building at the 11th-floor level, but a Ukrinform live entry at 17:43 said reports of debris hitting a residential building in Pechersk were not confirmed. Treat the building damage as unverified.

stories.title: Ukraine's military counted 205 clashes on the front on 18 November, mostly near Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka, while ISW assessed no confirmed advances by either side that day.
stories.summary: ISW said Russian attacks northwest of Huliaipole gained no ground and Ukraine counterattacked there; Russia launched 141 long-range drones overnight, 73 of them jet-powered.
stories.heat: ISW, Ukrinform, Kyiv Independent · velocity: steady
detail: Ukraine's General Staff reported 205 combat engagements on 18 November, with the heaviest Russian attacks on the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka axes, and said two attacks toward Dolynka and Yehorivka on the Huliaipole axis were repelled (Ukrinform). ISW's 18 November assessment says Russia's main effort is to encircle Ukraine's fortress belt from the southwest around Dobropillia and Pokrovsk, and that neither side advanced that day. The two counts use different sources and time windows.

stories.title: Amnesty International says RSF drone strikes on El Obeid that killed 37 civilians should be investigated as war crimes.
stories.summary: Amnesty's 18 November report covers nine RSF drone strikes on El Obeid and its surroundings between June and August 2026, which it says killed 37 civilians and injured 10. It says it is also investigating army drone strikes.
stories.heat: Amnesty, Middle East Eye, Radio Tamazuj, allAfrica · velocity: low, report-driven while the army advances in Kordofan
stories.about: El Obeid is the capital of North Kordofan, held by Sudan's army; the RSF besieged it until the army's recent offensive.
detail: Amnesty said it investigated nine RSF drone strikes on El Obeid and nearby areas from June to August 2026, killing 37 civilians and injuring 10, and called for war-crimes investigations. It said it is also investigating Sudanese army drone strikes that killed civilians. The report comes as the army and allied Darfur forces push west along the main highway toward En Nahud after breaking the RSF siege of El Obeid, Al Jazeera reported on 14 November.

sections.title: India
sections.blurb: Cyclone Akvan turns north towards the Andhra-Odisha coast, William and Kate end their visit with Modi, the BJP calls Rahul Gandhi "Mir Jafar" over his economy remarks, and Bumrah strikes on his Test return.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan has turned north and is now expected to cross the coast between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha around noon on 20 November.
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department says the severe cyclonic storm has peaked and will not become a very severe storm, but a red warning covers the north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts, with up to 21 cm of rain and a 1 m storm surge forecast (IMD bulletin via The Open Press, ETV Bharat).
stories.heat: ETV Bharat, Swarajya, The CSR Journal, Daily Jagran live tracker, The Open Press, IMD national bulletins · landfall about a day away · velocity: high, the forecast track moved north overnight
detail: New since the last edition, which gave a forecast landfall between Nellore and Tuni: Cyclone Akvan recurved on Wednesday 18 November and is now moving north. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) expects it to cross the north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri by around noon on Friday 20 November (ETV Bharat, IMD national bulletin No. 27 as reported by The Open Press).

The intensity forecast has come down. Swarajya reported on the afternoon of 18 November that the IMD expected a very severe cyclonic storm with winds up to 145 km/h by Thursday evening. The 2:30 am bulletin on 19 November dropped that: IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said the storm had reached peak intensity and there is "no possibility of further intensification". Landfall winds are now forecast at 90 to 100 km/h, gusting to 110 km/h, and the system should weaken to a depression by Friday night (The Open Press).

At 11:30 pm on 18 November the storm was about 480 km south-east of Narsapur and 600 km south of Gopalpur, moving north at about 5 km/h. A red message cyclone warning has been in force since 2:30 pm on 18 November. The IMD forecasts a storm surge of 0.5 to 1 m for West Godavari, Konaseema, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam, Ganjam and Puri, isolated rain of 21 cm or more over coastal Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha on 19 and 20 November, and 20 to 30 cm in Ganjam, Gajapati, Khordha and Puri on Thursday (The Open Press).

Preparations: Andhra Pradesh's disaster management authority says 13 NDRF and 11 SDRF teams are ready, and warning signals are hoisted at seven ports including Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam (Swarajya). In Odisha, Puri has 179 cyclone shelters open, 2,942 rescue boats on standby and a three-day halt to fishing and Chilika ferries; Rayagada has marked about 55 landslide-prone villages for pre-emptive evacuation, and Malkangiri is moving 285 women close to delivery into health facilities (ETV Bharat).
The IMD calls Akvan the third cyclone to threaten the Andhra coast within three weeks, which it describes as rare. No landfall, deaths or damage had been reported as of the morning of 19 November.

stories.title: Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales, met Prime Minister Modi in New Delhi on 18 November at the end of their three-day visit to India.
stories.summary: Modi praised William's Earthshot Prize and wrote that he looks forward to strengthening the India-UK partnership; Kensington Palace said the talks reflected "deep and enduring ties" (Reuters via Free Malaysia Today).
stories.heat: Ground News India top story, 28 sources (61% right-leaning), plus a second 28-source Ground News story on William's climate speech · Reuters, Yahoo, IndiaWest, The News · velocity: peaked, the visit is over
detail: The Prince and Princess of Wales met Narendra Modi at his residence in New Delhi on Wednesday 18 November, the last event of a visit that began on Monday 16 November (Reuters via Free Malaysia Today; IndiaWest). They discussed relations between Britain and India. Modi praised the Earthshot Prize, William's environmental award, and wrote on X: "Look forward to further strengthening the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership". He also referred to building on the recently implemented trade agreement between the two countries (Reuters).

A Kensington Palace spokesperson said the talks reflected "on the deep and enduring ties between the two countries", and the couple thanked India for an "exceptionally warm welcome" (Reuters). IndiaWest reports that the palace called the meeting a "fitting conclusion" to the visit.

Earlier on 18 November in Mumbai, William visited Dharma Productions, where Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor were present and dancers performed a song from Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham; Karan Johar said William "spoke extensively about the potential of Indian cinema". Catherine visited a maternity hospital in central Mumbai (Reuters).

The second big Ground News story on India today is William's speech at the Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai on 17 November, covered in the last edition. Reuters quotes him calling this a "pivotal moment for the planet" as heatwaves and floods become more frequent. Reuters notes this was Catherine's most high-profile trip abroad since her cancer treatment in 2024.

stories.title: The BJP called Rahul Gandhi "anti-India" and "India's Mir Jafar" after he told students at Columbia University that India is sitting on an "economic disaster".
stories.summary: Gandhi blamed unemployment, weak manufacturing and the education system; BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia accused him of defaming India abroad before Parliament's winter session, and Congress said the government cares only about perception management (The Newsmill, The Tribune, Asianet).
stories.heat: Ground News India: 25 sources, 48% right-leaning, third biggest India story · ANI, The Tribune, The Quint, The Federal, India TV, Asianet · velocity: high on 18 November, both parties still trading statements
detail: Speaking at a fireside chat at Columbia University's School of International and Public Affairs in New York, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said: "The blunt thing is that India is sitting on an economic disaster" (The Newsmill). Reports from ANI, The Tribune and The Federal say he pointed to massive unemployment, a broken manufacturing base and deep problems in the education system, and The Tribune reports him saying India's economic model "stopped giving results almost a decade ago". Outlets differ on the day: The Newsmill says Wednesday, Ground News's lead outlets say Tuesday 17 November in New York.

BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia replied on 18 November, calling the remarks "venomous" and Gandhi "India's Mir Jafar" and "anti-India". He said Gandhi "is a habitual offender. He will repeatedly go abroad, make baseless allegations, and defame India", and linked his foreign trips to the start of Parliament sessions, citing the upcoming winter session (The Newsmill; India TV headline). Mir Jafar, the commander who sided with the East India Company against the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey in 1757, is a common Indian byword for a traitor; the BJP used the same label for Gandhi over his London remarks in 2023 (Deccan Herald archive).

Congress hit back. Pawan Khera said the economy is in a bad state but the government is not bothered by that, only by Gandhi talking about it, and accused it of putting perception management ahead of real problems. Supriya Shrinate called the BJP's attack "boring and stale" on X (The Newsmill, Ommcom News).

Background: on the same day the Sensex and Nifty fell about 0.6% after a 13% rally in 12 sessions, while foreign investors had put about $10 billion into Indian shares in November (HDFC Sky). The BJP cited India's status as the fastest-growing major economy in its reply (Asianet).

stories.title: Jasprit Bumrah took three wickets on his Test return as India reduced New Zealand to 95 for 5 on the first morning of the Wellington Test.
stories.summary: Shubman Gill's India chose to bowl at the Basin Reserve on 19 November and left out Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja; Bumrah bowled Tom Latham for a duck in his first over (Outlook India, AP via Yahoo Sports).
stories.heat: Outlook India and ESPNcricinfo live blogs, AP via Yahoo Sports, Khel Now · first Test of the tour · velocity: rising, day 1 in progress at publication
detail: The first of two Tests began at the Basin Reserve, Wellington, at 3:30 am IST on Thursday 19 November; the second is at Hagley Oval from 27 November (Yahoo Sports). India won the toss and bowled. Their XI: KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal, Shubman Gill (captain), Rishabh Pant, Washington Sundar, Dhruv Jurel, Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj, Jasprit Bumrah and Prasidh Krishna, with no place for Mohammed Siraj or Ravindra Jadeja (Outlook India).

New Zealand were 60 for 4 at lunch and 95 for 5 after 35 overs at 7:08 am IST. AP says Bumrah removed Latham with the third ball of his return after about 12 months out of Tests. Outlook's scorecard gives Bumrah the wickets of Latham (0), Daryl Mitchell (1) and Tom Blundell (5), Akash Deep removing Rachin Ravindra (15) and Anshul Kamboj removing Devon Conway (4). Henry Nicholls was near a half-century. The day was still in progress when this edition was written.

stories.title: The Sensex fell 500 points to 82,032 on 18 November as investors took profits after a 13% rally in 12 sessions.
stories.summary: The Nifty 50 lost 0.63% to 25,227.95, Titan fell 5.3% and metals and consumer durables led the losses, while SBI and Cipla rose (HDFC Sky, Business Standard).
stories.heat: Business Standard, HDFC Sky, Kotak Neo, The Hawk · routine daily market coverage · velocity: medium, first fall after two days of gains
detail: New since the last edition's close of 82,532.19: on Wednesday 18 November the BSE Sensex fell 500.38 points, or 0.61%, to 82,031.81, and the NSE Nifty 50 fell 159.45 points, or 0.63%, to 25,227.95 (HDFC Sky; Business Standard gives the same Nifty figure). Thirteen of 16 sector indices fell, led by consumer durables (about minus 3%) and metals (minus 2.5%); the Nifty Midcap index lost 1.2%, and 2,800 BSE shares fell against 1,448 that rose.

Titan was the worst Nifty stock, down 5.3%, followed by HDFC Life, Hindalco and Bajaj Finance. SBI rose 2.38% and Cipla 2.13% after a US FDA inspection of its New York site ended with no action. HDFC Sky puts the fall down to profit-taking after the indices rose about 13% in 12 sessions, and says foreign investors have put about $10 billion into Indian shares so far in November. Brent crude fell 1.3% to $91.90 a barrel.

stories.title: The overhead wires on the 50 km Surat to Bilimora section of India's first bullet train line go live with 25,000 volts from 20 November.
stories.summary: The National High Speed Rail Corporation says it is the first section of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor to be energised and has warned people to treat the wires as live; the first phase, Surat to Vapi, is due to open around mid-2027 (ThePrint, Swarajya).
stories.heat: ThePrint, DT Next, Swarajya, Gujarat Samachar, Metro Rail News, NewsBytes · velocity: medium, milestone due tomorrow
detail: The National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) will energise both lines of the elevated Surat to Bilimora section in Gujarat from Friday 20 November, a first for the 508 km Mumbai to Ahmedabad high-speed rail project (Swarajya, ThePrint). Power will come from the grid through 14 traction substations along the corridor, and the NHSRCL has issued a safety warning that all overhead wires on the stretch must be treated as live from that date (Gujarat Samachar). Energising the wires is a step toward trial runs; reports give mid-2027 as the target for opening the first phase, between Surat and Vapi.

stories.title: Coal India's subsidiary Mahanadi Coalfields opens its share sale to the public on 19 November.
stories.summary: The issue is an offer for sale of 66.18 crore shares by Coal India, so Mahanadi Coalfields itself receives no money; bidding runs to 23 November, and listing is pencilled in for 27 November (IPO trackers).
stories.heat: IPO trackers (Finology, Choice, Chittorgarh, Kotak Neo), JournalArta · one of three issues worth more than Rs 10,000 crore together this week · velocity: medium, bidding opens today
detail: Mahanadi Coalfields, a Coal India subsidiary, takes bids from 19 to 23 November 2026, with allotment expected on 25 November and listing on the NSE and BSE on 27 November, according to IPO tracker sites. One tracker lists a price band of Rs 129 to 136 a share. The whole issue is an offer for sale of 66.18 crore shares by Coal India, so the company receives none of the proceeds. JournalArta reports that it leads three share sales worth more than Rs 10,000 crore together opening from 18 November. No subscription figures were available at the time of writing.

stories.title: Delhi's air quality is getting worse again, two days after Stage III pollution curbs were lifted.
stories.summary: NewsBytes put Delhi's AQI at 232 on 18 November, up from 204 the day before, with "very poor" air expected by Friday; a live monitor showed a US-scale reading of 336 late that evening (NewsBytes, aqi.in).
stories.heat: NewsBytes, aqi.in live dashboard · seasonal running story · velocity: rising slowly
detail: The last edition reported that GRAP Stage III curbs were lifted in Delhi-NCR on 17 November. Since then the air has worsened: NewsBytes reported a daily AQI of 232 (poor) on 18 November, up from 204, with vehicles responsible for about a quarter of fine particle (PM2.5) pollution, and said "very poor" conditions are expected by Friday 20 November. The private monitor aqi.in, which uses the US scale and so is not directly comparable, showed New Delhi at 336 with PM2.5 at 240 micrograms per cubic metre at 10:31 pm on 18 November.

stories.title: The BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal are reported to be close to renewing their alliance for the 2027 Punjab election, but neither party has confirmed it.
stories.summary: The Open Press reports the BJP wants 47 to 55 of Punjab's 117 seats; BJP state in-charge C R Paatil says the leadership will decide and denies meeting Akali chief Sukhbir Badal (ThePrint, The Open Press).
stories.heat: ThePrint, The Pioneer, The Open Press, The Tribune · velocity: medium, two days of reports
detail: The Akali Dal ended its 24-year alliance with the BJP in September 2020 over the farm laws, which were later withdrawn. The Open Press now reports that the two parties are close to a seat-sharing deal for the 2027 Assembly election, with the BJP seeking 47 to 55 seats and an announcement possible around Guru Nanak Jayanti, though not all of the BJP's Punjab unit supports it. C R Paatil told ThePrint the party leadership would decide on any alliance and said the BJP would win Punjab; an Akali spokesperson said the party would discuss an alliance only if one were formally proposed. A SCORE Punjab poll reported by The Pioneer finds AAP still ahead but weaker, and models a joint Akali-BJP vote share of about 29.4%.

stories.title: Leh and Kargil groups are boycotting Ladakh's 21 November municipal and panchayat polls and refuse talks with the Centre until the December hill council elections are postponed.
stories.summary: The Leh Apex Body has been on a hunger strike in Leh since 12 November; the groups say winter polls keep away residents who have left for the season, while the Home Ministry says it is open to talks at any time (The Wire, ETV Bharat, The Week).
stories.heat: Ground News India: smaller story, 1 source · The Wire, ETV Bharat, The Week, Deccan Chronicle, The Tribune · velocity: medium, polls in two days
detail: Polls to the Leh and Kargil municipal committees and to panchayats are due on 21 November, and elections to all eight Ladakh autonomous hill councils on 4 December (The Wire, The Week). The Ladakh Buddhist Association and two other Leh groups have announced a boycott of the November polls, and Kargil held a shutdown. The Leh Apex Body (LAB) and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) want the polls moved because many residents, students and older people leave for the winter, and they cite delimitation problems (Deccan Chronicle, ETV Bharat).

LAB chairman Chering Dorje Lakruk said the two groups will intensify their agitation in Leh and Kargil, and the hunger strike at NDS Park continues despite a ban on such protests by Ladakh's chief electoral officer. The dispute sits on top of the groups' wider demand for constitutional safeguards for Ladakh under the Sixth Schedule. Former MP Thupstan Chhewang has urged people to vote, and ThePrint reports 541 nominations for the hill council polls. The Home Ministry says it is open to dialogue with LAB and KDA at any time (The Tribune).

stories.title: Prime Minister Modi addresses the closing session of a Centre-state summit on social justice in New Delhi on 19 November.
stories.summary: The two-day summit at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan covers the Nasha Mukt Bharat anti-drug campaign, a single national scholarship portal, early help for disability and the Sugamya Bharat accessibility drive (PMIndia, Indianvartha).
stories.heat: PIB release carried by PMIndia, UNI, Webindia, The Newsmill · velocity: low, a scheduled event at 4:30 pm IST
detail: According to the Prime Minister's Office, Modi will speak at about 4:30 pm on Thursday 19 November at the valedictory session of the Departmental Summit on Social Justice and Empowerment at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan, New Delhi. Indianvartha describes it as the third in a series of departmental summits meant to coordinate the Centre and the states, with ministers and officials for social justice and disability welfare attending. Its four themes are the Nasha Mukt Bharat campaign against drug use, the One Nation One Scholarship portal, early intervention to reduce disability, and the Sugamya Bharat accessibility programme. No coverage of the speech existed when this edition was written.

sections.title: Cinema
sections.blurb: Ramayana passes Rs 1,500 crore worldwide by Sacnilk's count, Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is forecast at $160 to $190 million worldwide, Skydance reshapes the Paramount and Warner Bros film and TV studios, and Dhanush and Mammootty's O.M opens on Friday.

stories.title: Ramayana Part 1 passes Rs 1,500 crore worldwide after 14 days, by Sacnilk's estimate, while trackers still disagree on its India total.
stories.summary: Sacnilk puts the film at Rs 844.40 crore net in India and Rs 1,519.05 crore gross worldwide after Wednesday 18 November. Bollywood Hungama's lower count had it at Rs 778.50 crore net in India after 13 days.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available (the Reddit file was empty) · Sacnilk, Bollywood Hungama, Koimoi, India TV News, Filmibeat, News24 · velocity: high, the Rs 1,500 crore mark and the Dhurandhar comparison drive the day's headlines
detail: What is new since the 18 November edition (which carried Sacnilk's day 13 total of Rs 821.30 crore India net and Rs 1,483.50 crore worldwide): the second Wednesday, and the worldwide total going past Rs 1,500 crore.

Sacnilk estimates Rs 23.20 crore India net on day 14 (Wednesday 18 November), down 18.9% from a revised Rs 28.60 crore on day 13. Its 14-day totals are Rs 844.40 crore net and Rs 1,009.05 crore gross in India, Rs 510.00 crore gross overseas (Rs 8.00 crore of it on day 14) and Rs 1,519.05 crore gross worldwide. Hindi gave Rs 16.50 crore of the day from 17,661 shows, and average occupancy was 18.8%. India TV News also reported that the film crossed Rs 1,500 crore worldwide.

Other outlets count lower or higher. Bollywood Hungama reported Rs 25.79 crore net on day 13 (Tuesday 17 November) and a 13-day India total of Rs 778.50 crore net, of which Hindi was Rs 602.22 crore; it listed day 14 advance sales of Rs 11.15 crore but had not posted a final day 14 figure at writing time. Koimoi, according to search results (its page was blocked), had day 13 at Rs 31.1 crore and the total at Rs 849.18 crore. News24 gave a lower day 14 figure of Rs 18.46 crore, which was Sacnilk's earlier live estimate.

On the Dhurandhar comparison: on 17 November Bollywood Hungama headlined that Ramayana had passed Dhurandhar to become Bollywood's No. 2 worldwide grosser. Filmibeat gave Rs 840.2 crore as the Dhurandhar lifetime India figure that Ramayana would pass on day 14, without saying which Dhurandhar film it meant; Sacnilk's Rs 844.40 crore is above it. All these figures are trade estimates, not producer numbers.

stories.title: Deadline forecasts a worldwide opening of $160 to $190 million for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which opens on Friday 20 November.
stories.summary: Deadline expects $90 to $120 million in North America from 3,900 cinemas and at least $70 million abroad. The film holds 74% on Rotten Tomatoes from 101 reviews.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · Deadline (syndicated on Yahoo), Boxoffice Pro, Forbes, World of Reel, Rotten Tomatoes · velocity: high, previews began on Wednesday evening and the wide release is Friday
detail: What is new since the 18 November edition (which carried a North American floor of $80 million): Deadline's full global preview, published on 18 November, and the first reviews.

Anthony D'Alessandro of Deadline puts the worldwide opening at $160 to $190 million: $90 to $120 million in the US and Canada from 3,900 cinemas, and an international floor of $70 million from about 39,000 screens in 84 countries. NRG tracking says $80 million or more, while exhibitors expect "well north of $100M". Deadline gives the cost as about $150 million and says presales are well ahead of both Wicked films. Previews started at 6:30 pm on Wednesday 18 November in premium screens. Boxoffice Pro's panel forecasts $100 to $120 million domestic.

For comparison, Deadline lists The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes at $44.6 million domestic and $100.8 million worldwide at opening, and the franchise record, Catching Fire (2013), at $304 million worldwide.

Reviews are mixed to positive. The Rotten Tomatoes page showed 74% from 101 reviews when read; Forbes and World of Reel reported 69% when the embargo lifted on 17 November, and World of Reel gave a Metacritic score of 56. Francis Lawrence directs, with Joseph Zada as the young Haymitch and Ralph Fiennes as President Snow.
These are forecasts. The first preview numbers are expected on Thursday 19 November (US time).

stories.title: Skydance names Kira Goldberg, who leaves Netflix, and Don Granger as presidents of the Paramount Motion Picture Group, and Warner Bros distribution chief Jeff Goldstein retires after 48 years.
stories.summary: In the same reorganisation Jesse Ehrman becomes president of the Warner Bros Motion Picture Group. Paramount's Shaun Barber and Mark Viane take over distribution for both studios.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · Variety (via Yahoo), Deadline, The Hollywood Reporter, IndieWire, TheWrap · velocity: medium to high, the first big film-side shake-up since the Warner Bros deal closed
stories.about: Skydance, run by David Ellison, owns Paramount and completed its takeover of Warner Bros Discovery in October 2026.
detail: Variety's Rebecca Rubin reported on 17 November that Kira Goldberg and Don Granger will be presidents of Paramount's Motion Picture Group. Goldberg was most recently Netflix's film vice president for faith, holiday, young adult and family titles and worked on Don't Look Up and The Adam Project. Granger produced Skydance films including Mission: Impossible, Rogue Nation and The Old Guard 2.

Jesse Ehrman, a 20-year studio veteran who worked on A Minecraft Movie and Sinners, is promoted to president of the Warner Bros Motion Picture Group. Michael Ireland stays president of production and reports to him. A staff memo says the two studios "will remain distinct" and are meant to release 30 films a year together.

Jeff Goldstein, head of global theatrical distribution at Warner Bros Pictures, retires after 48 years and is expected to move to a consulting role, Variety reported; Deadline and TheWrap also reported his exit. Shaun Barber (domestic) and Mark Viane (international) of Paramount will run distribution for both studios and report to Josh Goldstine.

Other changes: Bill Damaschke leaves Warner Bros Pictures Animation to produce, Jennifer Dodge and Traci Balthazor oversee animation at both studios for now, and chief business officer Ted Lim leaves.

stories.title: Skydance will merge Warner Bros Television Group and Paramount Television Studios into one studio, called Warner Bros Television Studios, in early 2027.
stories.summary: Channing Dungey of Warner Bros TV and Matt Thunell of Paramount TV will run it as co-presidents. CBS Studios stays a separate unit.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · Deadline, The Hollywood Reporter, Variety, City News Service (KESQ), Screen Rant · velocity: high, announced 18 November
detail: City News Service, carried by KESQ on 18 November, reported that the two studio groups will combine into Warner Bros Television Studios, which launches in early 2027. Until then both keep working independently. Dungey and Thunell will report to George Cheeks, Skydance TV co-chair and chief content officer. BET Studios moves into the new studio; CBS Studios, led by David Stapf, stays separate and supplies the broadcast networks.

KESQ gives more than 100 active productions; other reports give more than 120 series, including HBO's Harry Potter, Netflix's Emily in Paris and CBS's Marshals. Cheeks called it "a formidable creative engine" and wrote in a staff memo, cited by The Hollywood Reporter, "We know there will be questions about what this means for individual teams." Several reports expect layoffs; no numbers have been announced.

stories.title: Neon releases the full trailer for Luca Guadagnino's Artificial, in which Andrew Garfield plays OpenAI chief Sam Altman.
stories.summary: The film, about Altman's firing and return in 2023, opens in select cinemas on Christmas Day and widens on 8 January. Amazon MGM dropped it in June and Neon picked it up.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · ABC Audio, Gold Derby (via Yahoo), Variety, IndieWire, Gizmodo · velocity: medium, trailer out 18 November
detail: ABC Audio reported on 18 November that the trailer shows Altman (Garfield) talking about AI over dinner with Ilya Sutskever (Yura Borisov) and the team finding that its chatbot can lie. In one exchange Mira Murati (Monica Barbaro) says "ChatGPT is generating misinformation" and Altman answers "Mira, I'm aware." Gold Derby lists Mark Rylance as Geoffrey Hinton and Ike Barinholtz as Elon Musk; Simon Rich wrote the script.

Amazon MGM Studios said on 19 June that the film "will be better served if it were released by a different studio"; Gold Derby links the decision to Amazon's deal with OpenAI. The film premiered at the New York Film Festival on 5 October.

stories.title: The Dhanush and Mammootty film O.M, now billed as O.M: Operation Mole, nears Rs 10 crore in worldwide opening-day advance sales before its release on Friday 20 November.
stories.summary: Filmibeat reports Rs 9.40 crore in worldwide day-one presales, citing tracker Jerin Georgekutty. The Week reports Rs 8.21 crore in India advance sales for the first four days.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · Filmibeat (several updates), The Week, Pinkvilla, Business Upturn · velocity: rising into release day
stories.about: O.M is a Tamil action thriller about red sandalwood smuggling, directed by Rajkumar Periasamy, with Dhanush, Mammootty and Sai Pallavi; it was announced as OM: Chapter 1, Udhiram.
detail: What is new since the 18 November edition (which carried Koimoi's day-one forecast of Rs 15 crore or more and a small early advance figure): the presales after wide booking opened. Filmibeat's Sharath Bose wrote late on 18 November that worldwide opening-day presales had reached Rs 9.40 crore, a figure the tracker Jerin Georgekutty shared on X. A separate Filmibeat report says it is Dhanush's best day-one advance in Kerala.

The Week, citing Sacnilk, reported Rs 8.21 crore gross in India for the first four days, including blocked seats (Rs 7.13 crore without them), from 5.65 lakh tickets across 6,156 shows in 287 cities. Day one accounts for Rs 4.24 crore of that. Tamil Nadu leads with Rs 4.06 crore. The film releases in Tamil, Telugu and Hindi.

stories.title: Sooraj Barjatya launches the trailer of Yeh Prem Mol Liya, with Ayushmann Khurrana and Sharvari, ahead of its release on 27 November.
stories.summary: The Rajshri family film runs 173 minutes and has a U/A 13+ certificate. In the trailer the groom says he will move into the bride's home after the wedding.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · Outlook India, Pinkvilla, Bollywood Hungama · velocity: medium, trailer launched 18 November
detail: Outlook India reported that the trailer was launched at an event in Mumbai on Wednesday 18 November. Prem (Khurrana) tries to win Purva (Sharvari), who hesitates because she feels responsible for her all-female household; Prem then announces he will move into her home after the wedding, reversing the vidaai tradition. The music is by Himesh Reshammiya, and the cast includes Supriya Pathak, Seema Pahwa and Anupam Kher.

The CBFC passed the film U/A 13+ on 17 November; Outlook says it is only the second Barjatya film as director to get a U/A rating, after Main Prem Ki Diwani Hoon (2003). It opens on 27 November against Gunmaaster G9, with Emraan Hashmi. Barjatya told the launch: "We have to keep showing up at the movies."

stories.title: The 57th International Film Festival of India opens in Goa on Friday 20 November with Pawel Pawlikowski's Fatherland, and Dhurandhar opens its Indian Panorama section.
stories.summary: The festival runs to 28 November under the theme "Stories Without Borders". Three Indian films, among them Kantara: A Legend, Chapter 1, are in the international competition.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · PIB (government release), IndiaBlooms, Goemkarponn, Bollywood Hungama, High On Films · velocity: rising, opening day is 20 November
detail: IndiaBlooms reported on 19 November that Fatherland, which won the best director prize at Cannes 2026, opens the festival. The Indian films in the international competition are Kantara: A Legend, Chapter 1 (Kannada), Paro: The Untold Story of Bride Slavery (Hindi) and The Kerala Story 2 Goes Beyond (Hindi). The Indian Panorama has 30 feature films, 20 non-feature films and five web series and opens with Dhurandhar. Some outlets wrote that Dhurandhar opens the whole festival; the government release and IndiaBlooms say it opens the Panorama.

Goemkarponn reports that Anthony Chen's We Are All Strangers closes the festival. Bollywood Hungama reported that Bharatbala's Banaras premieres there and that Back to the Future will be shown on Goa's beaches. The festival has tributes to Bharathiraja, K. Bhagyaraj and Nana Patekar.

stories.title: Disney expects to spend about $26 billion on content in fiscal 2027, 9% more than this year, after streaming revenue rose 19% in its latest quarter.
stories.summary: The rise covers sports rights, international programming and films. Disney plans to roughly triple its local originals over three years.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · The Hollywood Reporter, Deadline, Storyboard18, trade and finance sites · velocity: medium, earnings day story
detail: Storyboard18 reported on 18 November that Disney's fourth quarter (to 3 October) brought revenue of $25.9 billion, up 16%, and streaming revenue of $6.05 billion, up 19%, with streaming operating income of $824 million against $402 million a year earlier. The results include an extra 53rd week.
For fiscal 2027 Disney guides content spending of about $26 billion, up about 9%, The Hollywood Reporter and Deadline reported. The unified Disney+ app, with Hulu folded in, is due in December.

stories.title: Tabu joins Tunnel Men, a YRF Entertainment series for Netflix inspired by the 2023 Uttarakhand tunnel rescue.
stories.summary: It is her first Hindi streaming series. Shiv Rawail, who made The Railway Men, is showrunner.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · Bollywood Hungama, The Hollywood Reporter India, The Statesman, The Telegraph (t2) · velocity: medium, announced 18 November
detail: Bollywood Hungama reported on 18 November that Tunnel Men is a fictional drama drawn from the rescue of 41 workers trapped in the Silkyara tunnel in Uttarkashi in November 2023. It is the first project of Saugata Mukherjee as YRF Entertainment's head of content. No premiere date has been given. A separate film on the same rescue, Silkyara 41, is in development with Aamir Khan Productions and Kabir Khan.

stories.title: Brad Pitt says Ocean's 14 will not start shooting until late 2027, a further delay from the December 2026 start.
stories.summary: Pitt told Variety at the Cliff Booth premiere: "We're talking about sometime late next year." The shoot had already moved from June.
stories.heat: Reddit rank not available · Variety, MovieWeb, ComingSoon, Netflix Junkie · velocity: low to medium, reported 17 November and picked up through 18 November
detail: Variety's column of 17 November quotes Pitt at the 16 November premiere: "We're talking about sometime late next year." Filming had been due in December 2026 after a delay from June. George Clooney, Pitt, Julia Roberts, Matt Damon and Don Cheadle are set to return, with David Leitch directing. Some outlets infer a 2028 release; none has been announced.
